## Observation
A gating run in one session was killed by low memory (not a test failure). Investigation found three worktrees concurrently running full pytest-xdist suites (bug-lowcost-git-subprocess-timeout, fix-crane-fixture, plus the reporting session). Three concurrent suites on one host exhausted memory. Confirmed environmental cause: host memory contention, remedy applied was halving workers; fallback is serial. This is the same failure class as the 2026-09-06 host memory-exhaustion incident.

## Problem
make verify / make test default to PYTEST_WORKERS=4 (often raised to 8) per invocation, with no cross-session coordination. N parallel agent sessions => N*workers pytest processes, unbounded aggregate memory. Each agent behaves correctly locally; the host-level aggregate is the defect. Also noted: pgrep -f pytest matches ALL sessions' workers (text is not identity), so naive post-kill sweeps would kill other sessions' work — cleanup guidance must stay worktree-scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A mechanism bounds aggregate test-suite resource use across concurrent sessions on one host (e.g. cooperative host-wide concurrency cap for full-suite runs, worker autoscaling from available memory, or documented+enforced stagger protocol). Mechanism-ratchet: justify any new lock/env_var with a mechanism-ok marker referencing this ticket.
- [ ] Solution preserves parallel multi-agent development (serializing all verifies outright is unacceptable friction).
- [ ] A killed-by-OOM run is distinguishable from a test failure in guidance/output so agents apply the environmental-fault remedy instead of retrying blind or root-causing a phantom flake.
- [ ] AGENTS.md/docs updated: worktree-scoped process cleanup only (never pgrep -f pytest sweeps); reduced-worker/serial fallback protocol on memory kill.
- [ ] Regression evidence for the chosen mechanism.
compiled_state.title: Host memory exhaustion: concurrent agents each run fully parallelized pytest suites
